key_insight: A gate-level, non-variational quantum workflow amplifies high-quality solutions to the Closest String problem without instance-specific parameter optimization.
engineering_relevance: The automated circuit construction and analytical resource estimates provide a foundation for hardware experiments and classical benchmarking.
method: Encode candidate strings and evaluate their maximum Hamming distance to the reference strings.
Apply Non-Variational Quantum Walk Optimization Algorithm iterations to amplify low-distance candidates.
Scale the phase-separation parameter γ with problem size to mitigate excessive phase wrapping.
evidence_signal: Across all simulated problem sizes, the algorithm consistently amplified optimal and near-optimal candidates; estimated qubit use is O(nm log k) and circuit depth is O(pm log² n + pn log n).
watch_item: Simulation-based amplification does not establish practical quantum advantage; hardware noise and comparisons with classical solvers remain important evaluation needs.
paper_title: Designing Quantum Solutions to the Closest String Problem with the Non-Variational QWOA
